in order to an unvisited vertex. Self-loops never help; one vertex is the trivial path. Pruning cuts
only subtrees with no solution (an unvisited vertex unreachable, or left with too few
usable neighbours), so it keeps the order. Without a start the search is run again from
each vertex in turn until one succeeds, so a graph with no Hamiltonian path costs n
searches.

by Edmonds and Johnson’s algorithm, or nil when the graph has no edge or its edges are not
all connected. Isolated vertices are ignored.

as the shortest.
